D011-D018_h023.question_both:
I’ve always been a bit of a worrier, but over the past few months it feels like my brain is stuck on overdrive. At work, when I’m on the console, I’m supposed to be locked in on one caller, one screen, but my mind keeps jumping: “What if I miss something? What if I say the wrong thing? What if something happens and it’s my fault?” It’s like I’m constantly running through worst-case scenarios, and once that starts, I can’t shut it off, even when I’m off shift.

I’ve tried all the usual things—podcasts, music, scrolling my phone, going for walks—but the worry just keeps circling back. I’ll catch myself rereading the same line in an email three times because I can’t hold my focus. Even in conversations, I sort of zone out halfway through and realize I’ve missed chunks of what people are saying.

The job doesn’t help. Some of the calls I’ve taken still replay in my head sometimes, especially a couple of really bad ones, but I’m not sure if this all started because of that or if it just kind of built up over time. I just know I can’t seem to get my mind to settle.
D011-D018_h023.question_a:
I’ve been on edge for as long as I can remember, but it’s gotten a lot worse over the past couple of years. I’m a 911 dispatcher, so, yes, I’ve taken some awful calls—there’s one from a car crash that sticks with me—but what really gets me isn’t just that. It’s like I’m constantly bracing for every possible disaster, all day long, about everything.

I’m always running through “what if” scenarios: what if my mom gets sick, what if I mess up at work and someone dies, what if I lose my job, what if there’s something wrong with my car and I crash on the way home. Even when I’m off shift and just trying to watch TV or read, my brain jumps to the next worst-case scenario. I try breathing exercises, music, scrolling my phone, but the worrying just keeps coming back.

At work, my mind drifts even between calls. I’ll miss parts of what people are saying because I’m already worrying about the next emergency, or about my bills, or about getting old alone. It’s not just about that one bad call—it’s like my whole life is wrapped in this constant, uncontrollable worry.
D011-D018_h023.question_b:
It’s been about eight months now, since that one call, and I feel like my whole life is wrapped around it. I was on night shift, listening to this guy bleed out while I tried to keep him talking until units arrived. I could hear people screaming in the background and then… nothing. After that, I haven’t felt the same.

Most of my worrying now circles back to something like that happening again—on the job or even to my family. My brain won’t stop running through every possible “what if”: what if I say the wrong thing, what if a caller dies because I hesitate, what if my mom gets into a wreck and no one answers in time. I know it’s excessive, I tell myself to knock it off, distract myself with TV or scrolling, but the thoughts just push back harder.

At work, I can’t stay locked in on the calls like I used to. My mind jumps from the caller’s words to that night, to the worst-case scenario, and I have to reread the address three times. Even off shift, it’s like I’m still at the console, constantly bracing for the next disaster.
